body.statement: For every fixed nondegenerate bounded class \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\) containing the lower family, there exist \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\le\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\) the symmetric quotient pseudometric. The primary class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{Morse}}_{2,2,1}\) is justified directly by its \(C^2\) Hessian condition and has exponent \(3/4\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), the finite-type conditions imply almost-everywhere discrepancy and the conclusion agrees with exact componentwise recovery on the shared circular subclass of Liang et al. and Varıcı et al.; the strengthened smoothness, conditioning, separation, and attained-order assumptions are used only for the uniform nonzero-error frontier.
body.justification: The theorem names the critical-order recovery frontier in a symmetric quotient geometry and separates the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse headline from the novel general finite-type rate class.
body.gap: Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. prove qualitative exact recovery under almost-everywhere discrepancy; no cited Morse theorem supplies the \(k=2\) rate assumptions, and no comparator gives a symmetric law-based sharp exponent at isolated critical points.
body.consumer: Likelihood and score-based causal representation learners obtain a calibrated translation from population objective error to encoder error.
